al-ula.name: Al-Ula
al-ula.summary: An ancient oasis city in northwest Arabia on the incense trade route, once capital of the Lihyanites and near the Nabataean site of Hegra.

incense-trade-route.name: Incense trade route
incense-trade-route.summary: Ancient network of land and sea trade routes linking the Mediterranean with sources of incense, spices, and luxury goods, flourishing from about the 3rd century BC to the 2nd century AD.

kingdom-of-aksum.name: Kingdom of Aksum
kingdom-of-aksum.summary: A powerful trading kingdom in the Horn of Africa and South Arabia, founded around the 1st century, ranked among the era's four great powers, and one of the first states to adopt Christianity, in the 4th century.

qaryat-al-faw.name: Qaryat al-Faw
qaryat-al-faw.summary: Archaeological site in central Arabia, once capital of the Kingdom of Kinda, with remains of houses, markets, temples and wells; a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2024.

tuwaiq.name: Jabal Tuwaiq
tuwaiq.summary: An escarpment running about 800 kilometers through central Arabia's Najd plateau, along which the Saudi capital Riyadh and many historic settlements lie.

book-of-ezekiel.name: Book of Ezekiel
book-of-ezekiel.summary: A prophetic book of the Hebrew Bible recording visions of the exiled prophet Ezekiel in Babylon between 593 and 571 BCE.

sheba.name: Sheba (Saba)
sheba.summary: An ancient South Arabian kingdom in what is now Yemen, existing from around 1000–800 BCE until 275 CE, home to the Sabaean people and centered on the city of Marib.

raamah.name: Raamah
raamah.summary: A name in the Torah meaning 'lofty', listed as a son of Cush and later as a trading country linked to Tyre, usually placed in the region of Yemen.

faxian.name: Faxian
faxian.summary: A Chinese Buddhist monk who traveled overland to India starting around age 60 to collect Buddhist scriptures, journeying from 399 to 412 CE and writing an early account of Buddhist India.

hadhramaut.name: Hadhramaut
hadhramaut.summary: A region in the southern Arabian Peninsula, traditionally explained as meaning 'court of death,' stretching from the Empty Quarter desert to the Arabian Sea coast.

al-yamama.name: Al-Yamama
al-yamama.summary: A historical region in southeastern Najd, Saudi Arabia, that was a key theater in the Ridda wars after Muhammad's death.

al-kharj.name: Al-Kharj
al-kharj.summary: A governorate in Saudi Arabia's Riyadh Province, located about 83 km southeast of the capital.

ma-in.name: Minaeans
ma-in.summary: People of the ancient South Arabian kingdom of Ma'in in modern Yemen, one of four major ancient Yemeni groups, recorded from the 8th century BCE.

marib.name: Marib
marib.summary: Capital of Marib Governorate in Yemen and once capital of the ancient kingdom of Saba, possibly the biblical Sheba; it has recently absorbed nearly a million refugees from Yemen's civil war.

sirwah.name: Sirwah
sirwah.summary: A city in the ancient Kingdom of Saba on the Arabian Peninsula, its capital before Ma'rib took over, and site of a temple to Almaqah built around 700 BC.

najran.name: Najran
najran.summary: A city in southwestern Saudi Arabia, an ancient trade and agricultural center on caravan routes, notable for its pre-Islamic Christian community.

bir-hima-rock-petroglyphs-and-inscriptio.name: Bir Hima
bir-hima-rock-petroglyphs-and-inscriptio.summary: A rock art site in Najran province, southwest Saudi Arabia, settled during the Paleolithic and Neolithic periods (about 7000–1000 BC) and named a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021.
bir-hima-rock-petroglyphs-and-inscriptio.source_title: Bir Hima Rock Petroglyphs and Inscriptions

jubbah-saudi-arabia.name: Jubbah
jubbah-saudi-arabia.summary: An oasis city in Saudi Arabia's Ha'il Region, on an old caravan route, known for abundant agriculture and groundwater, and for nearby ancient rock art and lake deposits.

temple-of-awwam.name: Temple of Awwam
temple-of-awwam.summary: The main sanctuary of the Sabaean national god Almaqah, near ancient Marib in Yemen, active from the early 1st millennium BC to the 4th century AD; nearly a thousand inscriptions found there aid the region's history.

nabataean-kingdom.name: Nabataean Kingdom
nabataean-kingdom.summary: A political state of the Nabataeans controlling regional trade routes from the mid-3rd century BC until Rome annexed it in AD 106, renaming it Arabia Petraea.

wadd.name: Wadd
wadd.summary: The national god of the ancient Kingdom of Ma'in in South Arabia, later named in the Quran as one of five false gods worshipped before Islam.

bar-an-temple.name: Bar'an Temple
bar-an-temple.summary: A Sabaean temple near Marib, Yemen, dating to the 10th century BCE and dedicated to the god Almaqah; also known as the "Throne of Bilqis."

almaqah.name: Almaqah
almaqah.summary: National moon or sun god of the pre-Islamic Sabaean kingdom of Saba in Yemen, also worshipped in Ethiopia and Eritrea.

aelius-gallus.name: Aelius Gallus
aelius-gallus.summary: Roman prefect of Egypt from 26 to 24 BC, known for leading a failed military expedition into Arabia Felix under Emperor Augustus.

qal-at-al-bahrain.name: Qal'at al-Bahrain
qal-at-al-bahrain.summary: An archaeological site and fort in Bahrain occupied from around 2300 BC to the 18th century, once the capital of the Dilmun civilization and now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

augustus.name: Augustus
augustus.summary: Founder of the Roman Empire, ruling as its first emperor from 27 BC until his death in AD 14, and known earlier as Octavian.

baraqish.name: Baraqish
baraqish.summary: An ancient town in north-western Yemen inhabited since the Bronze Age, known to Greeks and Romans as Athlula; abandoned in the 1960s.

trajan.name: Trajan
trajan.summary: Roman emperor from 98 to 117 CE, one of the Five Good Emperors, whose conquests brought the empire to its greatest territorial extent; born in what is now southern Spain.

legio-iii-cyrenaica.name: Legio III Cyrenaica
legio-iii-cyrenaica.summary: A Roman legion originating under Mark Antony, later stationed in Egypt and Arabia Petraea, fighting campaigns against Nubians and Jews, with records into the 5th century.

bosra.name: Bostra
bosra.summary: Ancient city in southern Syria, the northern capital of the Nabataean kingdom and later a prosperous Roman provincial capital; today a UNESCO World Heritage archaeological site.

legio-vi-ferrata.name: Legio VI Ferrata
legio-vi-ferrata.summary: A Roman legion made part of Augustus's standing army in 30 BC, garrisoned in Judaea for two centuries; its symbol was the bull.

himyar.name: Himyar
himyar.summary: A South Arabian kingdom based in the Yemeni highlands that rose to dominate most of South Arabia by the late 3rd century CE, before falling to an Aksumite invasion in the early sixth century.

qataban.name: Qataban
qataban.summary: Ancient South Arabian kingdom in Yemen that existed from the early 1st millennium BCE to about the 2nd century CE, one of six major kingdoms of ancient Yemen.

rabbel-ii-soter.name: Rabbel II Soter
rabbel-ii-soter.summary: The last ruler of the Nabataean Kingdom, reigning from 70 to 106; his death led to Rome's annexation of the kingdom as the province of Arabia Petraea.

shammar-yahri-sh.name: Shammar Yahri'sh
shammar-yahri-sh.summary: A Himyarite king who was the first to hold the title "King of Saba', Dhu Raydan, Hadramawt and Yamnat" after uniting most of Yemen under his rule.

awsan.name: Kingdom of Awsan
awsan.summary: An ancient kingdom in South Arabia centered on the Wadi Markha, allied with Saba before being destroyed by it in the late 7th century BC and later resurging around the 2nd century BC.

mukarrib.name: Mukarrib
mukarrib.summary: Title used by rulers of ancient South Arabian kingdoms such as Saba, Hadhramaut, Qataban, and Awsan, whose holders led armies, built city walls, and issued official inscriptions.

aden.name: Aden
aden.summary: Ancient port city on Yemen's south coast, at the eastern approach to the Red Sea, serving since 2014 as the de facto capital of Yemen's internationally recognized government.

shabwa.name: Shabwah
shabwa.summary: The ancient capital of the Kingdom of Hadhramaut in South Arabia, once a royal city with multiple temples; its ruins lie in modern Yemen.

gdrt.name: Gedara (GDRT)
gdrt.summary: Gadarat (GDRT): King of the Kingdom of Aksum around 200 CE, the first Aksumite king known to have involved Aksum in South Arabian affairs.

grmt.name: BYGT
grmt.summary: Known as 'son of the najashi' during Aksumite king GDRT's reign, like his successor GRMT — though it isn't known whether that title meant crown prince or general.

zafar-yemen.name: Zafar
zafar-yemen.summary: Ancient capital of the Himyarite kingdom in the Yemeni highlands, which at its peak (110 BCE–525 CE) ruled most of the Arabian Peninsula.

ancient-south-arabian-script.name: Ancient South Arabian script
ancient-south-arabian-script.summary: An abjad writing system used in South Arabia from the late 2nd millennium BCE to the 6th century CE, ancestor of the Ge'ez script and sibling of the Phoenician alphabet.

sabaic.name: Sabaic
sabaic.summary: An ancient South Arabian language spoken by the Sabaeans from about 1000 BC to the 6th century AD, closely related to and possibly mutually intelligible with Arabic.

qatab-nian-language.name: Qatabanian
qatab-nian-language.summary: An Old South Arabian language spoken in the kingdom of Qataban between roughly 500 BC and 200 AD, known from about two thousand inscriptions.

ancient-north-arabian.name: Ancient North Arabian scripts
ancient-north-arabian.summary: A collection of scripts and languages used in north and central Arabia and south Syria from the 8th century BCE to the 4th century CE, distinct from the South Arabian scripts.

safaitic.name: Safaitic
safaitic.summary: A South Semitic script used by nomadic Arabs in southern Syria and northern Jordan to carve rock inscriptions recording names, genealogies and daily life.

hismaic.name: Hismaic
hismaic.summary: A variety of Ancient North Arabian script and its associated language, attested in northwest Arabia's Ḥisma region around the start of the Common Era, distinguished by lacking a definite article.

dadanitic.name: Dadanitic
dadanitic.summary: The script, and possibly language, of the oasis of Dadān (modern Al-'Ula) and the kingdom of Lihyan in northwestern Arabia, used in the later first millennium BCE.

nabataean-script.name: Nabataean script
nabataean-script.summary: A consonantal alphabet used to write Nabataean Aramaic and Arabic from the 2nd century BC, known from thousands of inscriptions found from Jordan to Saudi Arabia.

imperial-aramaic.name: Imperial Aramaic
imperial-aramaic.summary: A historical variety of Aramaic used as the language of administration under the Neo-Assyrian, Neo-Babylonian and Achaemenid empires, from about the 8th to 4th centuries BCE.

boustrophedon.name: Boustrophedon
boustrophedon.summary: A writing style in which alternate lines run in reverse, mirror-image directions, common on ancient Greek inscriptions and other early scripts.

namara-inscription.name: Namara inscription
namara-inscription.summary: A 4th-century inscription in the Arabic language, among the earliest known, prized as evidence of Roman-Arab relations and the shift from Nabataean to Arabic script; now in the Louvre.

shams-deity.name: Shams
shams-deity.summary: A sun goddess of Arabian mythology and patron deity of the Himyarite Kingdom, worshipped alongside gods of the Moon and the planet Venus.

marib-dam.name: Marib Dam
marib-dam.summary: An ancient dam near Marib in Yemen, first built around the 8th century BCE and regarded as an engineering wonder central to the Sabaean and Himyarite kingdoms.

nabataeans.name: Nabataeans
nabataeans.summary: An ancient Arab people of the southern Levant and northern Arabia whose trading network, centered on Petra, brought wealth until Rome annexed them in AD 106.

petra.name: Petra
petra.summary: Ancient city carved into rose-coloured sandstone in southern Jordan, capital of the Nabataean Kingdom from the 2nd century BC, famed for its rock-cut architecture.

herodotus.name: Herodotus
herodotus.summary: Greek historian and geographer (c. 484–c. 425 BC), called 'the Father of History' for his Histories, a detailed account of the Greco-Persian Wars and the peoples and lands around them.

boswellia.name: Boswellia
boswellia.summary: A genus of resin-producing trees; frankincense is extracted from the resin of Boswellia sacra and B. frereana.

tihamah.name: Tihamah
tihamah.summary: The Red Sea coastal plain of the Arabian Peninsula, running from the Gulf of Aqaba to the Bab el Mandeb strait.

arabia-petraea.name: Arabia Petraea
arabia-petraea.summary: A Roman province in what is now Jordan, created from the conquered Nabataean Kingdom in 106 AD under Trajan, with Petra as its first capital.

qedarites.name: Qedarites
qedarites.summary: An ancient Arab tribal confederation attested from the 9th century BCE, centred at Dumat al-Jandal, that expanded across northern Arabia before being absorbed into the Achaemenid Empire.

bostran-era.name: Bostran era
bostran-era.summary: A calendar system starting from 22 March 106 AD, used officially in the Roman province of Arabia Petraea after Rome annexed the Nabataean Kingdom, named for the city of Bostra.

nabataean-aramaic.name: Nabataean Aramaic
nabataean-aramaic.summary: The extinct Aramaic language used in inscriptions by the Nabataean Arabs, attested from the 2nd century BC and eventually giving rise to the earliest form of Arabic script.

lihyan.name: Lihyan
lihyan.summary: An ancient Arab kingdom in north-western Arabia, centered on Dedan, that flourished between the 5th and 1st centuries BC and controlled major caravan trade routes.

hejaz.name: Hejaz
hejaz.summary: A historical region of western Arabia, in modern Saudi Arabia, containing the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, the first and second holiest sites in Islam.

limes-arabicus.name: Limes Arabicus
limes-arabicus.summary: A desert frontier defense system of the Roman Empire stretching about 1,500 km from the Gulf of Aqaba, built to guard Arabia province and its trade routes.

khaybar.name: Khaybar
khaybar.summary: An oasis north of Medina in Saudi Arabia, inhabited by Jews before Muslims under Muhammad conquered it at the Battle of Khaybar in 628 CE.

tayma.name: Tayma
tayma.summary: A Saudi Arabian city and major oasis in Tabuk Province, on the trade route between Medina and Dumah, with a long history of habitation.

henotheism.name: Henotheism
henotheism.summary: Worship of one supreme god while not denying other deities may exist; the term was coined in the 19th century and later applied to Hinduism's many deities.

rahmanan.name: Rahmanan
rahmanan.summary: An epithet for a singular, monotheistic god used in South Arabia from the 4th to 6th centuries, adopted after the Himyarite Kingdom's rulers converted to Judaism.

hanif.name: Hanif
hanif.summary: In Islamic tradition, a pre-Islamic Arabian monotheist who worshipped the God of Abraham without following Judaism or Christianity; Muhammad himself is said to have been one.

a-tar.name: ʿAṯtar
a-tar.summary: An ancient Semitic deity identified with the planet Venus, worshipped in both male and female forms as an astral warrior god.

malkikarib-yuhamin.name: Malkikarib Yuhamin
malkikarib-yuhamin.summary: King of the Himyarite Kingdom in Yemen from 375 to 400, credited by some sources with converting Himyar's ruling class from paganism to Judaism.

paleo-arabic.name: Paleo-Arabic
paleo-arabic.summary: A pre-Islamic script used to write Arabic between the fifth and seventh centuries CE, found mainly in inscriptions across Syria, Jordan and Arabia, almost all mentioning only the god Allah.

wadi-musa.name: Wadi Musa
wadi-musa.summary: A town in southern Jordan, meaning 'Valley of Moses', located just a few kilometers from the ancient site of Petra.

obodas-i.name: Obodas I
obodas-i.summary: Nabataean king who ruled from 96 to 85 BC, celebrated for defeating invading Hasmonean and Seleucid forces and possibly worshipped as a god after his death.

al-lat.name: Al-Lat
al-lat.summary: Pre-Islamic Arabian goddess, once worshipped across the Arabian Peninsula, whose cult reached as far as Syria. According to Islamic tradition, her temple in Ta'if was demolished on Muhammad's orders in the seventh century.

al-uzza.name: Al-Uzza
al-uzza.summary: One of the three chief goddesses of pre-Islamic Arabian religion, worshipped with Al-Lat and Manat. A sacred stone cube at Nakhla near Mecca was part of her cult, and her temple was destroyed in 630 AD.

manat-goddess.name: Manāt
manat-goddess.summary: Pre-Islamic Arabian goddess, one of Mecca's three chief goddesses alongside her sisters Al-Lat and Al-‘Uzzá. She was the oldest of them.

marz-a.name: Marzēaḥ
marz-a.summary: Religious and social ceremony and institution of Northwest Semitic-speaking peoples in the Levant, linked to wine drinking and, in some evidence, to mourning and veneration of the dead.

kahl-god.name: Kahl
kahl-god.summary: Chief god of the city of Qaryat al-Faw, capital of the Kingdom of Kinda, from the 2nd century BC. He may be an Arabian version of the menacing, smiting gods of West Asia.

aretas-iv-philopatris.name: Aretas IV
aretas-iv-philopatris.summary: King of the Nabataeans from about 9 BC to 40 AD. After his daughter was divorced by Herod Antipas, he invaded Herod's territory and defeated his army.
